articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 3: Friday
articles.text: Round 3's Friday night slate delivered a stunning comeback, a coaching nightmare, and one of the cheapest buys of the season so far for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Here are my fantasy winners and losers from the action. ### Fantasy winners ##### Nikola Mirotic, Valencia Basket Signed as a late addition, [Nikola Mirotic] has looked right at home at Valencia, and fantasy-wise, he's back to his best. In the club's stunning comeback win at LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne, he posted 26.4 fantasy points, his highest total of the season, while climbing into third on the EuroLeague's all-time scoring list past Vassilis Spanoulis. Just 2.9% of fantasy managers have him on their rosters, and they're looking smart right now. ##### Patty Mills, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne Javier Gancedo had his "Dzanan Musa rule" for games in Bosnia and Herzegovina last season. Maybe it's time for a "[Patty Mills] rule" at LDLC Arena. Owned by just 1.8% of fantasy managers, the veteran guard finished with 25.0 fantasy points in Round 3, following 19.8 in Round 1 (also at home) and 9.0 in Round 2 (on the road). The pattern speaks for itself. ##### Marcus Bingham, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul The 0.8% of fantasy managers who heeded Javier Gancedo's advice in [his Fantasy Tips article] by rostering [Marcus Bingham] knew what they were doing. The Fenerbahce center erupted for 27.5 fantasy points on Friday night, making his 11.4-credit price tag look like a steal. Let's see if managers hold on to him for a trip to Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens next week. ### Fantasy losers ##### Oded Kattash, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv This is the first time I've featured a coach in the fantasy winners and losers column, but things have gone from bad to worse for Maccabi tactician Oded Kattash. A 90-67 drubbing on the road at Panathinaikos brought him -20 fantasy points, the worst mark of any coach in Round 3, following -10 in Round 2 and -5 in Round 1. The 4.6% of fantasy managers hoping for a miracle on Friday night ended up with egg on their faces. ##### Jaylen Hoard, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv At 14.7 credits, [Jaylen Hoard] was one of the most expensive forwards in fantasy heading into Round 3, so his -2.0 fantasy points was a big disappointment for the 1.1% of managers who had him on their rosters. Hoard has been a reliable option in past seasons, but his trajectory since a 20.0-point haul in Round 1 is worrying. ##### David DeJulius, Besiktas Istanbul It wasn't [David DeJulius]'s night against FC Barcelona, as he finished with -3.0 fantasy points in his team's home defeat. His 9.6-credit price looked enticing entering Round 3, even though he didn't feature in Round 2, but the 0.5% of fantasy managers who went for him will be regretting it.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 3: Thursday
articles.text: There were some monster performances on Thursday night and I hope you had some of the authors of those games on your [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. Of course, there were some stinkers, too. I hope you avoided those pitfalls. Here's a look at the best and worst of Thursday's performances: ### Fantasy winners ### [Theo Maledon, Real Madrid] To get 40 fantasy points is fantastic regardless of the price. To get it from a player who cost just 10 credits is amazing. That is what Theo Maledon did for the 9.2% of managers who invested in him this week. I am going to go out on a limb and say that most of the top scores in fantasy for Round 3 will come from managers who had Maledon, whose price is certain to rise before Round 4. ### [Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna] I am pretty certain that the number of fantasy managers who own Aliou Diarra is going to rise a lot in the next few days. It was 5.8% for Round 3. The Virtus center had a PIR of 22 in Round 2. Then he went off for 18 points and 14 rebounds for a fantasy score of 33 on Thursday. That’s a magnificent return for a center who cost 7.2 credits. ### [Mbaye Ndiaye, Olympiacos Piraeus] The athletic big man seems to have found a groove with Olympiacos and despite playing just 20 minutes off the bench, Mbaye Ndiaye scored 23 points on near-perfect shooting and grabbed 7 rebounds for a PIR of 29. That’s incredible value for the price of 7.5 credits. Congratulations to the 2.0% of managers who had Ndiaye for Round 3. #### Honorable mention: ### [Ognjen Dobric, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] It’s hard to put Ognjen Dobric in the same category as the other winners, who scored on average more than double what the Zvezda forward mustered. That said, Dobric cost much less (4.5 credits) and was owned by 5.9% of owners. That makes his 15.4 fantasy points pretty valuable! ### Fantasy losers ### Olympiacos Piraeus centers Nothing hurts fantasy managers more than foul trouble. [Tyrique Jones] got into foul trouble and barely played, featuring for a total of 3:22 minutes. He committed 4 fouls and that ended up in a PIR of negative-4. That is a crippling score for a center priced at 11.6 credits. At least Jones was only taken by 2.1% of owners. His fellow Olympiacos center [Donta Hall] is owned by 5.8% of owners and posted a negative-6! ### [Jared Butler, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] While Crvena Zvezda held odd Efes for the win, some of their key rotation players struggled and hurt their fantasy managers too. Jared Butler was the second-most owned Zvezda player at 8.5% and with a price 10.3 credits, his managers were surely confident that the second-year guard was going to deliver a lot more than a PIR on negative-2. His backcourt mate, [Chris Jones], came into Round 3 owned by 4.4% of managers, who paid 12.3 credits for him. Jones, though, hurt them with a score of 0. ### [Andres Feliz, Real Madrid] The Dominican slugger was a bit of a sleeper pick for some after averaging 9.5 points, 4 rebounds and 4.5 assists in his first two games. It sounded like a bargain for just 6.6 credits. So 14.8% of fantasy managers gave Andres Feliz a spot in their lineups for Round 3. And then he bottomed out with a negative-4 in the loss to Hapoel.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Forwards
articles.text: There's barely been time to catch a breath before Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] tips off. My advice isn't limited to forwards. Also check out my [guard] and [center] recommendations for Round 3. Here are the forwards I like in Round 3: ### Lefteris Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens I mean, this is a no-brainer. No cheap player is doing better than [Lefteris Mantzoukas], who has been absolutely extraordinary so far. In two games, he's averaging 13.0 points on 4-of-4 two-point shooting and 6-of-12 from three, 5.0 rebounds and a PIR of 15.5. He's been starting at power forward and making the most of his opportunity. If you don't have Mantzoukas, buy him now. ### Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas [Azuolas Tubelis] is still a bargain for his price range and has been excellent. His speed, high basketball IQ and versatility make him a perfect matchup against Paris, where he recorded his first career double-double last season. He's now averaging 14.5 points, 9.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists and a PIR of 22.5, and should keep helping Zalgiris all season long. ### Tadas Sedekerskis, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz It's good to see [Tadas Sedekerskis] fully healthy and playing like the effective player he's always been. He proved it against Valencia despite his team's 23-point loss, posting 16 points on 8-of-8 two-point shooting, seven rebounds and a PIR of 19 in just 22 minutes. Baskonia is set to bounce back at home in the Buesa Arena, and if that happens, Sedekerskis should be a big part of it. ### Jason Burnell, Armani Olimpia Milan There aren't too many mid-range options around 10 credits, so I'm finishing this piece with two of them. [Jason Burnell] had a rock-solid game in the Italian derby, with six points and 10 rebounds in under 17 minutes. Expect him to keep crashing the glass, playing with energy and hitting free throws to put together a solid PIR most nights. ### Conor Morgan, Besiktas Istanbul [Conor Morgan] looks confident in Besiktas's system, starting at power forward to pull the trigger from downtown and finish dunks off backdoor cuts. He's averaging 14.0 points on excellent shooting (80.0% on twos, 60.0% on threes), 2.5 rebounds and a PIR of 13.5. As long as he keeps finding good shots, Morgan will keep knocking most of them down.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Guards
articles.text: With Round 2 in the books, it's time for a quick turnaround as Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] already tips off tonight. My advice isn't limited to guards. Also check out my [forward] and [center] recommendations, too. Here is who I like at guard in Round 3: ### Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul After playing just seven EuroLeague games across the last two seasons, [Scottie Wilbekin] looks like the player fans used to love and opponents used to fear. He put on a show against one of his former teams, Maccabi, finishing with 20 points on 4-of-5 three-point shooting, three assists and a PIR of 18 in under 23 minutes. Right now, Wilbekin looks like one of the biggest bargains in the game. ### Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade It's been a while since a EuroLeague player collected 10 steals across his first two games of a season, and [Luca Vildoza] is doing exactly that. Despite coming off the bench, he's posting strong numbers: 11.5 points on 85.7% shooting from three, 2.5 assists, 5.0 steals and a PIR of 15.0. He faces Olympiacos, one of his former teams, in Round 3. Just go for him. ### Theo Maledon, Real Madrid It's a bit surprising to see Real Madrid sitting at 0-2, and that's exactly why I think *Los Blancos*' players are worth a look in Round 3. Real faces Hapoel in Sofia, a rematch of last season's playoffs, and [Theo Maledon] has been playing well so far, averaging 10.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.5 fouls drawn for a PIR average of 14.0. All-around production always pays off. ### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket Valencia set a new all-time scoring club record with 111 points against Baskonia, and it should keep pushing the pace against ASVEL. [TJ Shorts] had 10 assists and just one turnover in Round 2, posting a PIR of 20 while taking only eight field goal attempts. Going back to France should bring back good memories, which only makes him a more attractive, top-class choice this week. ### Sterling Brown, Zalgiris Kaunas I spoke about Zalgiris's guard situation before Round 2: Dovydas Giedraitis and Maodo Lo each finished with a negative PIR, Carsen Edwards had a solid game, and [Sterling Brown] was the only one who truly overperformed. I'd expect more of the same as Zalgiris visits a fast-paced Paris side in Round 3. He averaged a PIR of 18.5 across two games against Paris last season, well above his season average of 11.0.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Centers
articles.text: Round 2 wrapped up fast, and Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is already here. My advice isn't limited to centers. Also check out my [guard] and [forward] recommendations for Round 3. Here is who I like at center in Round 3: ### Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas You might think Paris's fast-paced game would be too much for a big man like [Jonas Valanciunas]. Think again. He's been unstoppable so far, averaging 12.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 2.0 blocks and a PIR of 22.5. Arvydas Sabonis's last season, 2003-04, was the one before I created the game. Is JV the closest thing to "Sabas" in Fantasy? Probably. ### Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna Fantasy managers have been complaining to me for two weeks about the lack of cheap, good centers. Well, if that's your thing and you watched the Italian derby, now you know. [Aliou Diarra] finished that game with 15 points on 6-of-9 two-point shooting, seven rebounds, four blocks and a PIR of 22. He also had a PIR of 10 against Fenerbahce, and now faces an Olympiacos team still missing Nikola Milutinov. ### Tonye Jekiri, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade That center situation at Partizan is hard to figure out, but here's what I know: [Tonye Jekiri] is a steady choice with a high floor. He'll always grab some rebounds, block a shot or two and score efficiently. In Paris, he had 15 points, seven rebounds and a PIR of 22, hitting 7-of-10 two-point shots. With Joffrey Lauvergne and Derek Willis out, I like him here. ### Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens I don't like to repeat myself much, but if you don't have [Mathias Lessort], it's probably hurting your Fantasy team. He's on a mission to outpower every big man he faces, and he's up against Maccabi next, a team he hasn't always had the best time against. I know the "former player revenge" theory isn't written in stone, but Lessort has been on fire lately and should keep it going. ### Marcus Bingham, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul After showing hints of what he's capable of during the Euroleague Basketball SuperCup, [Marcus Bingham] had an excellent EuroLeague debut with Fenerbahce: 12 points on 5-of-7 shooting, three rebounds, a block and a PIR of 15 in under 16 minutes. Expect rebounds, plenty of blocked shots and the occasional three-pointer from him going forward. At his price, Bingham is a good choice.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Wednesday
articles.text: - [Tuesday's Fantasy Challenge winners and losers] Just two games took place on Wednesday as Round 2 came to a close, and plenty of [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers were hoping to find a savior, or hoping their opponents didn't. Some smart managers found top performers at a cheap price; others watched their expensive bets flop. Here are Wednesday's Fantasy winners and losers from Round 2's second night. ### Fantasy winners ##### Devon Dotson, Besiktas Istanbul At 9.9 credits entering Round 2, [Devon Dotson] was priced as a mid-tier guard, but boy did he pay off for the 0.5% who had faith in him. He returned 26.4 fantasy points in Besiktas's 93-109 win at Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv. Expect his price to rise after this start to life in the EuroLeague. ##### Lefteris Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens At this point, it's no longer a surprise. [Lefteris Mantzoukas] would be a prime Breakout Fantasy Star candidate if that award existed. Valued at 4.8 credits entering Round 2, he finished with 20.9 Fantasy points in Panathinaikos's 102-79 win over LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne. Some 16.1% of you clearly heeded [Frankie and Javi's advice from the podcast]. Well done. ##### Nikos Rogkavopoulos, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens Mantzoukas got the acclaim, but [Nikos Rogkavopoulos] reminded everyone what he's capable of, finishing with 19.8 Fantasy points in the Greens' beatdown of ASVEL. The 6.1% who owned the 4.4-credit forward, despite him sitting out Round 1, must be feeling good about themselves, especially since I expected Konstantinos Mitoglou to be the one who broke out. ### Fantasy losers ##### Isaac Bonga, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens You'd expect [Isaac Bonga] to be a consistent fantasy performer at Panathinaikos, but that hasn't been the case: 1.1 points in Round 1, then 3.3 in Round 2. At 11.0 credits, the 5.6% who own him must be weighing whether to jump ship. Bonga's always been a better real-life player than a fantasy one, despite his improvement in fantasy last season, so his value could easily keep sliding. ##### Jae Crowder, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne Another pricey forward at 10.2 credits, [Jae Crowder] came back down to earth on Wednesday. After an impressive Round 1 debut, the 5.0% riding that wave got just 6.0 fantasy points as ASVEL fell at Panathinaikos. With a home game against Valencia Basket up next, it's worth watching if he bounces back. ##### Keaton Wallace, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv It's been a tricky start for [Keaton Wallace]. After -3 fantasy points in Round 1, at least 3.0 in Round 2 is progress, but not what you want from a 10.2-credit price tag. As a newbie, he's owned by just 0.6% of managers, and I don't expect that to climb until he finds his feet. There are better options at that cost, or cheaper.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Tuesday
articles.text: Eight of Round 2's 10 games were played on Tuesday night, so the performance of players in those games on your [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] teams carries a lot of weight. Did you get the low-priced studs to boost your lineup? Did you get burned by high-priced flops? And nearly as important, who did those you compete against have? Let's break down which players sent your heart singing and which ones left you searching for a paper bag to cover your head with. Here are Tuesday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners ### [Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna] What was I thinking! I researched Aliou Diarra. I believed in him. I had him on my roster for Round 1. And then I dropped him. What a fool I was! Diarra erupted for 15 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks, amassing a PIR of 22. If you are among the 2.1% of fantasy managers who had him, you got great value for a mere 6.6 credits. He’ll be more expensive by Round 3. ### [Dylan Osetkowski, Valencia Basket] A PIR of 20 is certainly not unheard of for Dylan Osetkowski, but it’s not common either. He had reached that number 4 times in 62 EuroLeague appearances entering this week. And then on Tuesday he scored 12 points on near-perfect shooting for a PIR of 20 off the bench in a blowout win over Baskonia. A fantastic performance for a 7.7-credit player. ### [Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade] With a line of 16 points and 6 steals, Luca Vildoza defied logic to help Partizan win in Paris. He earned 23.1 fantasy points for the 5.3% of owners bold enough to pay the 7.8-credit price tag on the Argentinian guard. It was the first time in 15 games that Vildoza had achieved a PIR of at least 20. How long until he does it again with Partizan? ### Fantasy losers ### [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid] There is no way around it. If you were among the 5.4% of fantasy owners to roster Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot this week, you are in a bad place. It’s a trifecta of doom. His negative-10 PIR dooms your team this week. The fact that it came from a player you paid 12.4 credits for adds salt to the wound. And the relatively high loss in credits (it could be as high as a full credit!) you will see factored into TLC’s price before Round 3 dooms you a second time. Yikes! ### [Dario Brizuela, FC Barcelona] Oh, the fantasy gods can be so fickle! A week ago, we were celebrating those who had the foresight to pay 6.4 credits for Dario Brizuela as he racked up 17.6 fantasy points for just 6.4 credits. His price even rose 0.4 credits. Did you then sell him? Few did. Brizuela is owned by 8.9% of managers in Round 2 and he did not reward them. The Basque Mamba was held scoreless and posted a PIR of negative-8. Another tough pill to swallow. ### [Tyrique Jones, Olympiacos Piraeus] Sometimes fantasy owners (myself included) are naïve enough to think that when a star is sidelined, someone else can step into his minutes and perform. And sometimes we strike gold. Other times, we see Tyrique Jones give us 1.1 fantasy points after we paid 12.1 credits hoping he would dominate with Nikola Milutinov out. I say “we” to be kind. I didn’t make this mistake. But 2.2% of owners did. Better luck next time, my friends.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2: Who to hold, buy, or sell
articles.text: The Round 1 of EuroLeague Fantasy is behind us, but after just one round, it is difficult to draw any definitive conclusions about players. A player’s performance and value can change significantly from round to round, so it is important to look at the bigger picture, including form, minutes, role within the team, and the upcoming schedule. That is why in this feature we will track EuroLeague players across the HOLD, BUY and SELL categories: players worth keeping, players whose value could rise, and players for whom it may be the right time to make a change. EuroLeague Fantasy Prices 2026-27: All 326 Player Credits HOLD Moses Wright – Milano – 13.7 credits Milano arguably boast the most favorable upcoming schedule in the entire EuroLeague. Over the next stretch, they will lock horns with Virtus, Baskonia, and Maccabi Tel Aviv – matchups where their frontcourt should flourish. While Moses Wright was completely contained in the opening round against Partizan and finished with a single-digit fantasy score, one quiet game does not alter his long-term outlook. He remains the central focal point around whom Milano’s tactical system will revolve this season. A massive number of fantasy managers placed their trust in him for Round 1, and selling him now would be premature. He is a primary hold for Round 2. Joel Parra – Barcelona – 6.7 credits Selected by roughly 30% of fantasy managers in the opening round, Joel Parra delivered a massive disappointment by finishing with zero fantasy points and suffering a 0.3 credit price drop. However, dropping him immediately based on a single outlier would be a mistake. Parra remains the premier budget option in his price range, slotted into a vital role as one of Barcelona’s primary anchors. Outside of that Round 1 bump, he consistently posted index ratings above 20 throughout preseason and Liga Endesa . His role and talent remain intact – hold him for Round 2 and expect a swift rebound. Arijan Lakic – Partizan – 4.0 credits Arijan Lakic is an absolute must-have asset at his minimum 4.0-credit valuation. Securing a baseline role of around 20 minutes per game at the basement price tier offers unparalleled roster flexibility. With Derek Willis sidelined, Partizan’s already depleted rotation shrinks even further, locking in Lakic’s court time and usage. His price tag is heavily insulated with massive upward mobility, making him a prime candidate to appreciate in market value. Holding him is a no-brainer until he approaches the 4.5 to 4.8 credit threshold – until then, keep him firmly locked in your lineup. EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2 Tips: Best Player Picks & Head Coaches BUY T.J. Shorts – Valencia – 15.1 credits Alongside Milano, Valencia hand managers one of the most enticing fixture runs over the next two rounds, locking horns with Baskonia at home before traveling to face Asvel. The up tempo, high-possessions game state expected in both encounters fits T.J. Shorts ’ game like a glove. If you passed on him in Round 1, bringing him in now is essential. He immediately demonstrated that Valencia is his team, taking full ownership as the focal offensive leader and engine. Expecting him to comfortably eclipse 20 fantasy points across both matchups is a realistic baseline given his dominant, high-usage workload. Dinos Mitoglou – Panathinaikos – 5.9 credits With Juancho Hernangomez questionable for the upcoming double round due to a groin issue, Panathinaikos’ already tight rotation upfront gets even thinner. That leaves head coach Zeljko Obradovic relying heavily on a frontcourt core of Mathias Lessort , Guerschon Yabusele , and Dinos Mitoglou . At a budget price tag of just 5.9 credits, Mitoglou represents extraordinary value. He is in line for an expanded role with a clear path to 20+ minutes of playing time while Panathinaikos navigate a highly favorable stretch of games. Given his scoring and rebounding potential, he is one of the top low-cost BUY targets on the market for Round 2. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Centers
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] has just started! Not off to a good start? Don't worry, I am here to help you! You have four trades, so let's use them wisely. This may be the help you need to bounce back! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 1. Jonas Valanciunas was a slam dunk as he marked his return to the EuroLeague with 26.4 fantasy points and a gain of 0.4 credits. Kevarrius Hayes was also a clever pick as he went for 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.2 credits, while Allan Dokossi was nearly as good with 12 fantasy points and a gain of 0.1 credits. Moses Wright hurt a lot of us with just 9 fantasy points, which caused him to lose 0.3 credits and I was too high on Austin Wiley, who ran into foul trouble, scored just 4.4 fantasy points and lost 0.3 credits. My advice is not limited to big men. Go see my [guard] and [forward] recommendations. Here is who I like at center in Round 2: ### Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.0 credits) It is a very simple decision to make: if you have the credits, you should go for [Mathias Lessort]. First, he is a T2 player, so if Vezen... if your captain doesn't play well, then you have a great choice with a very high floor. Lessort was at his very best in Round 1 with 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks and 9 fouls drawn against Paris. Who will stop him from now on? ### Dan Oturu, Hapoel Tel Aviv (14.9 credits) [Dan Oturu] had an outstanding first quarter against Bayern with 9 points and 8 rebounds. He looked on his way to be MVP of the Round, but slowed down and Hapoel didn't win. He finished that game with huge numbers: 20 points on 10-of-11 two-point shooting, 12 rebounds and 2 blocks for a PIR of 32. Oturu is Coach Itoudis's number one choice at center. He should be on your team. ### Olek Balcerowski, FC Barcelona (8.3 credits) If you need a cheaper option, then you can go for [Olek Balcerowski], who had a couple of really good performances last week. He opened the EuroLeague season with a bang: 10 points and 4 rebounds for a PIR of 14 against Efes. Balcerowski did even better in the Spanish League with 21 points and 6 rebounds for a PIR of 30. Josh Nebo is out, so it's Balcerowski's time in fantasy. ### Johannes Voigtmann, FC Bayern Munich (7.9 credits) Yes, Bayern plays against Fenerbahce, but it comes off a big win against Hapoel on [Johannes Voigtmann]'s go-ahead three-pointer. He made the most of his 19 minutes on the floor with 10 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists for a PIR of 17, while making few mistakes. Voigtmann has a lot of talent and experience, and comes off a game-winning shot. At his price, he is a good option. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.5 credits) Last week, we talked about Partizan centers and how they would split minutes. Well, with Joffrey Lauvergne sidelined, [Kevarrius Hayes] and Tonye Jekiri are seeing more playing time and making the most of it. Hayes started in Round 1, finishing the game against Milan with 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting and 3 rebounds for a PIR of 12. Definitely not bad for 7.5 credits, right?

articles.text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague is underway and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. I know, Round 1 left some disappointments but now, you have four trades to improve your team. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Guards
articles.text: Round 1 of the 2026-27 EuroLeague seasons is in the books and with it the first round of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge], too. Now we are heading into the first double-round week of the season. It is time to check the schedule, look for Turn 2 players who will deliver in Round 2, and reload your rosters before the next deadline, on Tuesday at 18:00 CET. My Round 1 picks were pretty good and three of them gained 0.2 credits! They were, TJ Shorts, who scored 22 fantasy points, Nigel Williams-Goss with 15.4 points and young Mario Saint-Supery with 11 fantasy points. Meanwhile Sylvain Francisco had 19.8 fantasy points and went up 0.1 credits. Alas, Matteo Spagnolo accounted for 7 fantasy points and his price remained the same. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration for Round 2. I have made my picks at [forward] and [center], too. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.9 credits) I said we would focus on T2 players, which means there will be a lot of Panathinaikos players in all fantasy articles this week. Panathinaikos is the heavy favorite to win both games at Telekom Center Athens. [Sylvain Francisco] signed for ASVEL early in the off-season and ended up playing for Panathinaikos. It should be a special game for him, so keep an eye on him. ### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (14.5 credits) This is almost a no-brainer. [Carlik Jones] was the Round 1 MVP and even though Partizan plays twice on the road this week, it faces fast-paced teams in Paris and Bayern. He should keep leading Partizan the way he did in Round 1, making Jones a must for all fantasy teams. If you got him in Round 1, don't sell him. If you missed him, he is still affordable, so go for it. ### Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (7.7 credits) In recent years, [Scottie Wilbekin] may not have been the best fantasy player, but at 7.7 credits, it is hard to ignore a player of his caliber. He had a solid Round 1 game against Valencia, getting a PIR of 13, and goes against Maccabi in Round 2. Wilbekin remains Maccabi's all-time top scorer in the EuroLeague with 1,801 points. Talent and motivation always go well together! ### Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne (5.3 credits) This is a surprise that few saw coming. [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada] took over in Round 1, leading ASVEL to an 84-74 home win over Maccabi with 14 points, 5 assists and a PIR of 17 as a starter, playing over 21 minutes. An isolated good game? Think again. Fodzo Dada also played almost 21 minutes in French League action, too. All aboard the Fodzo Dada train! ### Dovydas Giedraitis, Zalgiris Kaunas (4.3 credits) Owned by just 1.3% of fantasy managers at the moment, [Dovydas Giedraitis] is a very cheap option that should allow you to afford other players. [Nigel Williams-Goss] is sidelined for Zalgiris, which opens the door for Giedraitis, who started and played 20 minutes in the Lithuanian League on Sunday. Giedraitis is a cheap get for all fantasy managers.

articles.text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. Round 2 has a particularity, cause only 4 teams will have their matchup in Turn 2, so that means we have to think about players to captain in those 4 teams, to be able to have a decent captain in both turns. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. I also tend to not repeat the ones I recommended last round, so take all this into account. 🧠GUARDS Chris Jones (12.6 cr): On the roster analysis for Zvezda I already talked about him possibly nearing his prime on this Zvezda, and I was not far from the truth. He has started the season in a really great way, showing leadership as playmaker, but also confience on the scoring side. He might not be the one with the biggest usage, but I think that will increase gradually. Theo Maledon (10 cr): We predicted Theo being one of the players taking a step forward with Pedro Martínez and that’s what we’ve seen until now. He did an amazing preseason, now he has started the season in an unbeatable way, being the best player in both games played so far (EL & ACB). Devon Hall (8.5 cr): We’ve already seen the usage coach Poetta will give him, so that added to his capacity to contribute from every aspect of the game, makes him a great option. He might not be the best scorer, but I think he’s a pretty safe player, as he probably won’t get a -5 FPTS game. Maodo Lo (7.1 cr): After finding out the 2-weeks injury of Nigel Williams-Goss, the first direct replacement that comes to my mind is Maodo Lo, who should be the one to get his minutes. He might not be on his best career moment, but he has the quality and talent to put up a really great performance as playmaker. Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada (5.3 cr): He seemed to have a really quick adaptation to top-level basketball and a pretty decent usage to be that young, so it looks like a great option on that price. He’ll play in Turn 2, so that makes it even better as a Round 2 choice, even though teammates like Patty Mills could be the musts. 🎯FORWARDS Kameron Taylor (12.6 cr): His last season was really good, but he started this one even better, so I think on a team where he might be one of the scoring references during all the season and with his rebounding capacity, the ceiling is really far from where he’s right now. Alec Peters (12 cr): While Garrison Mathews remains sidelined, he might be one of the best Forwards available in Fantasy terms. His playing time is already pretty high (30 mins) and will keep being like this as long as Mathews is injured. He just need to contribute a little bit more in rebounding and defensively to become the ultimate choice. Kessler Edwards (10 cr): He’s a really complete PF that already got a massive performance on this season Italian Supercup vs Milano (25 EFF). He can get +10 FPTS without even scoring, so imagine the potential if he gets a great game in terms of scoring, on a game that will be easier for him than Fener. Dinos Mitoglou (5.9 cr): He started the season in a really great shape, with the confidence he was missing last season, so being that cheap and while NHD keeps sidelined, he could have really great performances as he’s good on rebounding, but also on mid-range and 3pt shooting. 🗼CENTERS Mathias Lessort (15 cr): He’s an obvious choice, but especially this round against ASVEL and being probably the best captain option for Round 2, Turn 2. He seems to be again nearing his prime and that means the ceiling of this guy is still really far from 15 credits, so it might be time to select him. O. Balcerowski (8.3 cr) : As Nebo keeps sidelined, he’s performing on surprising numbers in both EuroLeague & ACB first games, so he might be one of the best mid-price centers right now. Great rebounding capacity and accompanied by pretty good playmakers in terms of creating spaces for him to end up alone under the basket. Jasiel Rivero (7.5 cr): Two great rounds ahead for Valencia facing 2 of the “weakest” teams on paper and especially Baskonia being a really bad frontcourt defender. That makes Jasiel a really good option to consider in cheap options, as he could be in advantage under the basket quite a lot of times. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! • Οι αγωνιστικές υποχρεώσεις συνεχίζονται με αμείωτο ενδιαφέρον και γρήγορο ρυθμό στη EuroLeague.
• Πολλοί παίκτες-κλειδιά αναζητούν αντίδραση μετά τις χαμηλές πτήσεις της προηγούμενης αγωνιστικής.
• Οι απουσίες και οι τραυματισμοί δημιουργούν ευκαιρίες για οικονομικές επιλογές (budget picks) στο παιχνίδι.
• Η διαχείριση του μπάτζετ και η σωστή επιλογή αρχηγού παραμένουν καθοριστικές για τη βαθμολογία.
• Αρκετές ομάδες αντιμετωπίζουν αγωνιστικά προβλήματα και αλλαγές στη σύνθεσή τους ενόψει των νέων αναμετρήσεων.
